transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It's getting really frustrating. My kitchen table is completely covered with things—my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and all these half-finished lists. I'll sit there looking at it all, not knowing which thing I'm supposed to do first, and then... well, before I know it, the whole day is just gone.
Has this kind of difficulty organizing things and tasks been a pattern for you your whole life, or is this something new that started more recently?

It's been a pattern my whole life, really. Even when I was a little girl, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always forgetting my books and my homework... and they constantly had to give me reminders to finish my seatwork before I could go outside. So, no, it's definitely not a new thing.
Over the past two weeks, have you been feeling down, depressed, or noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy?

No, I haven't really felt depressed or anything like that. I still enjoy going to church and the senior center when I can actually get myself out the door. It's just the frustration of not getting things done that bothers me, not a feeling of being down or sad.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, like forgetting conversations you just had, misplacing things more than before, or having trouble learning new information?

I wouldn't say I'm forgetting conversations or having trouble learning new things. But misplacing things... yes, though it feels like I've always been that way. I am forever hunting for things I literally just had in my hand. 

It happens constantly. I'll put down the car keys or my reading glasses, turn around, and they're just gone. I spend so much of my day searching for appointment cards, or recipes for the church supper, or... or the folder I need to take to the doctor’s office. So I don't know if it's a new memory problem, exactly, but keeping track of the things I was just holding is a daily struggle.

Have these problems with organization and misplacing things caused noticeable difficulties in more than one area of your life — for example, both at home and in other settings like work, church activities, or social situations?

Yes, it definitely affects me in more than one place. It's gotten to the point where I actually had to step down from leading a big event at the senior center recently. I just couldn't keep all the moving parts organized. And at home... well, my daughter has started double-checking my bills and my appointments. She just doesn't trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore, and honestly, I can't blame her.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or find yourself talking excessively or interrupting others in conversations?

I don't really interrupt people or talk too much, but... well, I do fidget quite a bit. Even when I’m at church or trying to sit politely in a meeting at the senior center, I catch myself rubbing my hands together, tapping my foot, or clicking my pen. I shift around in my seat so much that people actually look over at me sometimes. I just can't seem to sit completely still.
